summary:
I checked the formal core of the setting, search, caution, imitation and coherence sections and their appendices line by line, against the verified sources T1, T2 and L3, their Verification logs, and the round-2 re-verification. No fatal error: all key results I re-derived are correct as stated and proved. That covers lem:search:stepwise, thm:search:tonk and its PAC corollary, the purification lemma, the commitment lemma and the doctrinal paradox. It covers thm:caution:vs, :esc, the single-schema, tagged, untagged and Bell bounds, and :ville with its tightness numbers (recomputed: 0.9889, 0.9907, 0.781). It covers thm:imitation:coupon, the untagged, noise and necessity results, and cor:imitation:systematic. It covers thm:coherence:halving, :robust, :post, :cpc, :ipc, :popper, the trilemma, :carnap, :rank, :telltale and :residue(ii). Every \leanok name in these sections is a real declaration in lean/InfLearn.

What remains is 1 major and 16 minor issues:
- The major one: the explicit finite basis in the proof of Thm 6.15(a) (thm:coherence:cpc) has no axiom for ⊥ or ⊤. These are primitive constants of the paper's own language, so "⟨D⟩ = Cn₂" fails as written. Round 2 flagged this and it was not repaired.
- Thm 4.7(ii) and Thm 4.9 give a negative bound in a degenerate case.
- Several overclaims or stale remarks that round 2 flagged survive in the paper: the Table 6 caption uses the wrong quantifier; Thm 6.29(d) claims "not identifiable at all" beyond its proof; an RCF question is called "open" though a short argument settles it; Thm 6.38(iii) lists non-r.e. completions and says the T_k "cannot be discriminated"; the Clark's-completion remark needs a qualifier; a parenthetical in Prop 6.8(b) needs the worst-case hypothesis; §3.3 drops the complete-calculus hypothesis in its heading.
- Lean-tag bookkeeping: prop:coherence:adm's tag is attached to its IPC part (c) but formalizes only half of (b), and the result is missing from tab:lean:map. lem:imitation:cautious is also missing from the map. The lem:coherence:bag, thm:coherence:robust and thm:coherence:post tags overstate or understate their scope.
- Minor typos, duplicate bib keys, and one appendix that cites T1 instead of the paper's results.

The full report is at /home/user/AI-works/inferential-learning/research/paper-review/math-core.md.

issues.location: Proof of thm:coherence:cpc, paragraph 'Explicit finite bases' (and the parenthetical in coherence.tex Thm 6.15(a))
issues.problem: The paper's formulas include primitive constants ⊥ and ⊤ (setting.tex §2.1; also the Lean language), and the coherence datum is A_0 ⊬_h ⊥. The displayed basis is the Łukasiewicz axioms, the ∧/∨ →-axioms and MP, with no axiom about ⊥ or ⊤. So ⊥ behaves as an unsubstitutable atom: ⊢¬⊥, ⊢⊤ and ⊢⊥→p are not in ⟨D⟩, and the proof's conclusion 'Hence ⟨D⟩=Cn_2' is false in the paper's language. Round-2 re-verification flagged this (T2 'Thm 3.3(a), revised example basis', item (1)). It was not repaired, and Lean does not formalize the finite-basis clause.

issues.location: Caption of tab:coherence:rank ('they exclude only meanings realizing no certified position')
issues.problem: Wrong quantifier. A certification of ⟨A|D⟩ excludes every meaning that fails to realize that particular position, so a meaning is excluded as soon as it misses some certified position, not only when it realizes none. Example: certifying ⟨χ,¬χ| ⟩ excludes BV. Round 2 flagged this (T2 Sec 4.2 reading (i)).
issues.proposed_fix: Replace the second caption sentence with: 'Coherence \emph{certifications} are positive data about meanings: certifying $\pos AD$ excludes exactly the meanings that do not realize $\pos AD$ (for the empty position, only $V=\emptyset$), and adding $\valtop$ to a meaning never makes it fail a certification.'

issues.location: thm:coherence:telltale (d): 'Without structurality BV is not identifiable in the limit at all, even with the coherence datum'
issues.problem: The proof, and Lean BV_not_BC_learnable, cover text plus the single target-independent datum ⟨ | ⟩. With all target-certified positions supplied, text plus certifications is an informant (cf. prop:coherence:informant). Then ⟨χ,¬χ| ⟩ separates BV∪{v'_χ} from BV and the class becomes identifiable. 'At all' therefore overclaims. Round 2 flagged this (T2 Thm 4.4(d)).
issues.proposed_fix: Replace with 'Without structurality $\BV$ is not identifiable in the limit from text plus the coherence datum $\pos{\ }{\ }$, or any other target-independent certifications:'. Append: '(If every target-certified position is supplied, text plus certifications is an informant, as in \Cref{prop:coherence:informant}, and this obstruction disappears.)'. Adjust the 'Non-learnability' paragraph in app-coherence.tex the same way.

issues.location: Reading after prop:coherence:complete: '(Whether a fixed finite family of contexts suffices for RCF is open.'
issues.problem: Round-2 re-verification (T2 Prop 3.11(c)) notes this is settled negatively. Each context in a finite family 𝒜 defines a semialgebraic set over ℚ whose components contain points with algebraic coordinates of degree ≤ D(𝒜). A term forced to be a root of f is constant on components, so it takes such a value. For even d > D′(𝒜), the rule t^d=1+1 ▷ t>0 (Eisenstein, degree-d root) therefore never fires in a designated context or from ∅. It is coherent on 𝒜 yet unsound (c=−2^{1/d}).
issues.proposed_fix: Replace the sentence with: '(No fixed finite family of contexts suffices: the rule $t^{d}=1+1\step t>0$ with $d$ even and large enough never fires in any context of the family, because points of semialgebraic sets defined over $\mathbb Q$ have algebraic coordinates of bounded degree, so it is coherent on the family but unsound; this observation is due to the second-round referee.)', or delete the sentence.

issues.location: thm:coherence:residue (iii) (and app-coherence.tex proof of (iii))
issues.problem: §6.3 fixes 'Hypotheses are r.e. theories', but (iii) lists 'PA+¬Con(PA) and its non-standard completions', which are not r.e. Also, 'the sound T_k ... remain, and cannot be discriminated' overstates thm:coherence:turing. Distinct T_j, T_k are separated by text; what fails is identification of the chain together with T_ω. Round 2 flagged both points (T2 Thm 6.4(iii)).
issues.proposed_fix: Replace (iii) with: '$\mathcal G$ deductive closure, $\hstar=\PA$, $\Ac=\{\emptyset\}$: $\Alt$ is the set of all consistent closed extensions of $\PA$ (the r.e. ones, if hypotheses are r.e.), e.g. $\PA+\neg\Con(\PA)$, whose completions (not r.e.) have only non-standard models. Designating all finite sets of true sentences removes exactly the unsound ones; the sound $T_k$ of \Cref{thm:coherence:turing} remain, and by that theorem no learner identifies them together with $T_\omega$ from text plus true-context coherence.' Make the matching change in the appendix.

issues.location: ex:coherence:survivors (4), last sentence: 'The per-law converse is not Clark's completion, which is consistent there.'
issues.problem: This holds only if rain and sprinkler are treated as abducibles, i.e. only the head wet is completed. Clark's full completion also makes the clause-less predicates false (¬rain, ¬sprinkler), which is inconsistent with A={wet}. Round 2 flagged this (T2 §6 example 4).
issues.proposed_fix: Replace with: 'The per-law converse is not Clark's completion \citep{clark1978negation}: completing only the head $\mathit{wet}$ (with $\mathit{rain},\mathit{sprinkler}$ abducible) gives $\mathit{wet}\leftrightarrow\mathit{rain}\vee\mathit{sprinkler}$, which is consistent there.'

issues.location: Reading after tab:coherence:rank: 'A testable prediction ...: imitation plus a contradiction penalty yields consistent but noncommittal reasoners.'
issues.problem: thm:coherence:carnap and thm:coherence:rank show only that such data do not exclude gappy valuations ('provably free to settle on'). They give no reason to expect that training yields them, so 'yields' is an overclaim.
issues.proposed_fix: Replace with: 'A testable question for language-model training: imitation plus a contradiction penalty does not rule out consistent but noncommittal reasoners; whether training drifts toward them is empirical.'

summary:
I re-checked the 15 named results of the two-tier, simplicity and existence sections by hand against the repaired T5, T6 and T7 files, including both repair rounds of T7. All 15 are mathematically correct as stated, with the repaired versions used throughout. That covers thm:twotier:main and its N_1 formula in both modes, prop:twotier:practice, thm:twotier:burnin under (OE), thm:twotier:depth, cor:twotier:cpc, thm:twotier:arith(a)-(f), thm:simplicity:kink, separable, validation (ii)-(iii) and division, and thm:existence:points, bilindenbaum, arity, omega and computability. I also recomputed every quoted constant numerically (N_1 = 16, eps_E = 0.0144, p < 0.1421, the note's rates and window, the guard rates, 1/omega(2) = 2.409, and the two-point counterexamples); all reproduce. Every Lean name cited in these sections exists and is sorry-free in audit-output.txt.

The problems are at the edges of the results.
- existence.tex says almost nothing in the section is formalized and omits Lean tags for six results, contradicting app-lean.tex and the Bilateral and Specker modules.
- intro.tex and philosophy.tex claim exact convergence for complete decidable theories without the realizability proviso, which twotier.tex itself says is unestablished.
- twotier.tex line 412 says "over N the converse holds", the opposite of the lemma it cites.
- The "true enough" definition in existence.tex is degenerate as stated. The round-2 re-verification flagged this and it was never repaired.

The rest are minor: a missing uniqueness hypothesis in thm:simplicity:validation(i), a misplaced Lean tag, DLO completeness, an overclaim about learning first-order logic, a proof gap for "asserted forever" in thm:twotier:arith(b), Reading paragraphs that drop the collateral and the residue, an incomplete list of unrefereed round-2 repairs, and the counting-sequent scope needing negation coherence. The full report is in /home/user/AI-works/inferential-learning/research/paper-review/math-advanced.md.

issues.location: line 101, Table tab:intro:answers, row 'A setup that provably works for formal mathematics'
issues.problem: The row says the learner 'is sound and exactly convergent for classical propositional logic and complete decidable theories (cor:twotier:cpc, cor:twotier:decidable)'. cor:twotier:decidable is conditional on realizability, and twotier.tex line 410 says that hypothesis 'is not established for the listed theories'. It fails for a literal forall-E schema, whose lgg is over-general (ind_lgg.py). Without realizability TTL is only eventually sound under the depth schedule, and exactness fails.
issues.proposed_fix: Replace the cell with: "\textbf{Yes, with explicit scope.} The two-tier learner (\cref{thm:twotier:main}) is sound and exactly convergent for classical propositional logic (\cref{cor:twotier:cpc}). For complete decidable theories the residue is empty, and exact convergence holds provided the target calculus is realizable as first-order patterns (\cref{cor:twotier:decidable}); this is open for the usual axiomatizations of RCF, ACF$_p$ and Presburger arithmetic, and fails for a literal $\forall$-elimination schema. It is Popperian for arithmetic, with sharp impossibility results beyond $\Sigma_1$ (\cref{thm:twotier:arith})."

Consistency and rendering review, checked against the current sources: intro, abstract, philosophy and open were revised at 06:31–06:34, so I rebuilt them in a scratch copy. That build has 0 errors, 0 undefined references or citations, and 265 pages.

**Macros:** none of the 87 macros defined with \providecommand/\newcommand in sections/*.tex has two different definitions. The only one already defined before its section is \Fm, and the definition is identical.
